correctness.rationale: Every proper ideal lies in the radical; its intersections with uniserial branch modules are uniquely chain tails; multiplication by each branch generator forces the residual coordinates into one socle layer. The absence of coordinate axes exactly captures intersections. Gaussian inclusion-exclusion counts the resulting subspaces. The branchwise perfect balanced bilinear form yields a genuine dimension-reversing ideal involution. Direct RREF closure tests independently match eight finite field configurations; no finite test is used as a general proof.

evidence: Moore 2007 provides structural results for Ext and resolutions over arbitrary local fibre products.
Conca–Römer 2007 proves a generic-initial-ideal relation over standard graded fibre products.
Kassel–Reutenauer 2015 covers ideal codimension enumeration in Laurent polynomial algebras, with its main results on two-dimensional tori.
The two-branch complex nodal-curve ideals are described in the 2023 Mathematics Stack Exchange answer; its claim does not extend to arbitrary branch number or count ideals over finite fields.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The generality of Moore is homological, not a theorem about every ideal or its dimension distribution. Conca–Römer concerns ideals defining the fibre product and their generic initial ideals, not all ideals inside the resulting quotient. The torus ideals in Kassel–Reutenauer are finite-codimensional ideals in an infinite-dimensional Laurent ring, not subideals of this Artinian monomial ring. The two-branch normal form is covered, while a comprehensive uniserial-submodule lattice theorem might imply the full result, and is retained as a residual risk.

originality.rationale: The two-branch nodal ideal classification over the complex field is covered by a 2023 mathematical discussion and is explicitly credited rather than claimed as new. The all-branch exact dimension enumerator, multibranch axis-avoiding Grassmannian parametrization and dimension-reversing radical duality are not stated or logically implied by the other inspected sources. Classical Gaussian subspace counting is not independently claimed as original. Historical priority remains provisional because unlocated general uniserial-module formulae could subsume the full package.
residual_risks: The two-branch normal-form special case is prior work over C and is excluded from any originality claim.
The general classification of submodules of direct sums of non-isomorphic uniserial modules (or a Hall polynomial) might subsume the normal form and its counting consequence.
The direct-product paper was read only at publisher-abstract level; its ring setting differs and no decisive implication was observed, but its full arguments were not inspected.
Semantic and web searches are non-exhaustive; publication priority is provisional.

value.rationale: The dimension-enumerator for the entire ideal lattice of a multi-branch Artinian fibre product is a natural exact invariant in commutative algebra. It distinguishes nonmonomial ideal strata and all branch lengths; its dimension-palindromicity is structurally explained by radical self-duality even when the ambient local ring has socle rank greater than one. The result applies uniformly to arbitrary fields for classification and every finite field for arithmetic counts, not an arbitrary finite slice.
